existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Armitage and Guldi place Robert Darnton’s episodic cultural histories within their criticism of the narrowing horizons of anglophone microhistory.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Joint 2014 chapter names the works as examples while conceding microhistory’s original ability to link scales, public popularity and critical gains. This does not say the author’s entire career lacked public engagement. Hunt’s 2015 response expressly disputes the characterization; her target is the related 2015 article. The cited Davis 1975/Darnton 1984 books remain unread.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Darnton praises Vovelle’s testamentary research but questions whether declining ritual proves dechristianization and how fully the change is explained.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Own1974review final paragraphs distinguish decline from extinction and suggest that abandoning baroque rites could signify religious purification. He also finds socio-economic change too general and some explanation circular, while praising the method as a major historical advance and acknowledging similar explanatory limits in other great theses. This is not a rejection of quantitative research or proof Vovelle asserted Christianity vanished; original monograph unread.

named_group_routes_inspected.relationship: Geertz’s interpretation of symbolic practices becomes a resource for cultural history
named_group_routes_inspected.evidence_note: Hunt’s primary 1984 p. 87 supplies a named reception example; the existing political-history edge specifies that use. Darnton’s original acknowledgments add a specific Princeton co-teaching mechanism with Geertz; his introduction names Lévi-Strauss and acknowledges archival mediation. Davis (revision 1.143): she acknowledged reading Geertz ‘eclectically’ among other anthropologists and co-teaching a course with him at Princeton (Haskins Lecture, 1997, pp. 14, 19, read in full); the checked passages establish no specific adoption of thick description, and her anthropological route is recorded on the anthropology → natalie_zemon_davis edge. None of this certifies all anthropological routes into cultural history. Earlier review (to revision 1.142): Davis was recorded as ‘an earlier proposed example whose direct reception is not established by the passages checked here’.

named_group_routes_inspected.relationship: Bourdieu’s distinction between practical sense and scholastic reason (cited 2003) and his account of social difference (2007 dialogue); Certeau restored the space of readers’ appropriation, though Chartier rejects reading his “poaching” as absolute freedom
named_group_routes_inspected.evidence_note: His own words. 2003 article, read in full: to think "cette irréductibilité de l'expérience au discours", historians could rely on Foucault's distinction and on "celle établie par Bourdieu entre « sens pratique » et « raison scolastique »" (¶25, n. 26: Méditations pascaliennes, 1997). 2007 dialogue with Darnton, read in part in Portuguese translation (MATRIZes 5:2, 2012): social difference "não decorre apenas dessa tradição da história social da Annales, decorre também … ao trabalho de Pierre Bourdieu" (p. 164); no contradiction between Bourdieu's sociology of cultural production and McKenzie's sociology of texts (p. 166); "De Certeau, entre outros, restituiu este espaço" between constraints and readers' appropriation, but "seria um erro acreditar que esta liberdade é absoluta" (p. 167). In 1988 he recorded five radio dialogues with Bourdieu, published as a book in 2010 (presentation, p. 162; Prismas bibliography). Named resources with qualifications, not adherence to a school.

named_group_routes_inspected.relationship: Later studies of the mobility of texts across attributions, printed versions, forms of publication, genres and translations: the lost Cardenio between Cervantes and Shakespeare (2011) and Éditer et traduire (2021), in their reviewers’ accounts
named_group_routes_inspected.evidence_note: Mediated: the books are unread. Boucheron's review of Cardenio (Books & Ideas, 2014; consulted through WebFetch extraction; selected quoted passages recorded; full text not collated): its problem is "the discrepancy between the mobility of texts and the stability of authorial names"; Boucheron expects the claim that the author function took its final form in the eighteenth century to "provoke debate, particularly among Medievalists": an anticipated objection, not a later controversy investigated here. Jouhaud (Prismas 26, 2022, pp. 236–237, read) quotes Éditer et traduire on "las cinco modalidades que suministran a las obras su movilidad" (attribution, printed variants, forms of publication, genres, translation). Chartier's own 2020–2021 Collège de France report (read via WebFetch extraction) describes research "vouées à comprendre les raisons de la mobilité des textes". Prismas's bibliography dates the books (2011; 2021). A contribution to the history of publishing and circulation within intellectual history; Darnton's separate strand membership is unchanged.
named_group_routes_inspected.map_label: The mobility of texts, 2011–2021, per reviewers

named_group_routes_inspected.relationship: Distinguishes microscopic reading of evidence from merely choosing small subjects, seeking general historical questions whose particular answers need not be mechanically generalizable (2019).
